extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how to require restriction/election and how to treat double patenting issues in U.S. national applications under 35 U.S.C. 111, including special rules for Markush claims, nucleotide sequences, transitional applications, rejoinder, and copending applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'Independent' and 'Distinct'
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'independent' inventions as unrelated (no disclosed relationship in design, operation, or effect) and describes 'related but distinct' inventions (disclosed as connected in design, operation, or effect but nevertheless distinct if claimed inventions are not connected in at least one of design, operation, or effect and at least one is patentable over the other).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives examples (combination and subcombination, process and apparatus, process and product) and explains that 'distinct' permits division among dependent/related inventions; warns that case law uses terms variably and decisions must be read carefully. References MPEP §§ 806.05(c), 806.05(j), 806.06, 808.01 for examples and two-way tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction is the practice of requiring an applicant to elect a single claimed invention for examination when two or more independent and/or two or more distinct inventions are claimed in an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites 35 U.S.C. 121 and 37 CFR 1.142; indicates restriction can apply to combinations/subcombinations, product/process, or species within a genus. See MPEP § 802.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: When Restriction Is Proper
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement for restriction may be proper only if the claimed inventions each could support separate patents and they are either independent or distinct as claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-prong test: (A) inventions must be independent or distinct, and (B) there would be a serious burden on the examiner if restriction is not required. If the search/examination of all claims can be made without serious burden, the examiner must examine them on the merits even if they cover independent or distinct inventions. See MPEP § 803 and § 803.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for Restriction Between Patentably Distinct Inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: For patentably distinct inventions, a restriction requirement is proper only when (A) the inventions are independent or distinct and (B) there would be a serious burden on the examiner without restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must provide reasons and/or examples to support conclusions (need not cite documents in most cases). When inventions can be viewed as related in two ways, both applicable distinctness criteria must be demonstrated. An express admission that inventions would be obvious over each other means restriction should not be required (In re Lee). See MPEP § 803.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serious Burden on the Examiner (Serious Burden Test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction may be required when failure to restrict would place a 'serious burden' on the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prima facie showing of serious burden can be made by explanation of separate classification, separate status in the art, or a different field of search as defined in MPEP § 808.02. Applicant may rebut this showing with evidence. If no serious burden exists (examiner can search/examine all claims), claims must be examined on the merits. See MPEP § 803.01 and § 808.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners Must Provide Reasons/Examples
rubrics_metrics.description: When making a restriction requirement, examiners must set forth reasons or examples supporting the restriction conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although reasons/examples are required, examiners generally need not cite supporting documents. Where plural inventions are capable of being viewed as related in two ways, both applicable criteria must be demonstrated. See MPEP § 803.01 (Guidelines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review by Examiner With At Least Partial Signatory Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Only examiners with appropriate signatory authority may sign Office actions containing final requirements for restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid issuance of improper requirements, only an examiner with permanent full signatory authority or temporary full signatory authority may sign final Office actions containing a final requirement for restriction. Examiners with permanent partial signatory authority may sign non-final Office actions containing a final requirement. See MPEP § 803.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush Claims — Unity and Provisional Election
rubrics_metrics.description: Markush-type claims recite alternatives (e.g., 'selected from the group consisting of A, B, and C'); members should ordinarily belong to a recognized class, and unity exists where members share a common utility and a substantial structural feature essential to that utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Markush members are few or closely related so the entire claim can be searched without serious burden, examiner must examine all members. If a Markush claim encompasses at least two independent/distinct inventions, examiner may require a provisional election of a single species prior to examination. Use form paragraphs 8.01 or 8.02 as appropriate. After election, the Markush claim is examined with respect to the elected species; if elected species is unpatentable, claim and elected species are rejected and non-elected species held withdrawn. If elected species is allowable, examination of the Markush claim is extended as necessary. See MPEP § 803.02 and § 809.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional Application Restriction Rules (37 CFR 1.129)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special transitional rules apply to applications pending for at least 3 years as of June 8, 1995: restriction or divisional filing requirements generally shall not be made or maintained after June 8, 1995, except under specified exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If transitional exceptions do not permit restriction, applicant is notified and may elect inventions and pay the fee (37 CFR 1.17(s)) for each additional invention, confirm prior election and pay fee, or file a petition traversing the requirement. Examples of applicant actions that can prevent restriction prior to April 8, 1995 are stated. Form paragraph 8.41 may be used to notify applicant. Refunds are available if linking or generic claim allowance removes withdrawal of nonelected claims. See MPEP § 803.03 and subsections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional Application — Refunds for Linking or Generic Claim Allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: In transitional applications where the applicant paid the fee for additional inventions, applicant may request a refund of the fee if (a) a linking claim is found allowable and rejoins inventions, or (b) a generic claim becomes allowable and embraces nonelected species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifies examiners to refund fees if (a) linking claim allows rejoining per MPEP § 809 and § 821.04(a) or (b) nonelected species are fully embraced by an allowable generic claim per MPEP § 806.04(d), § 821.04. See MPEP § 803.03(a) and § 803.03(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nucleotide Sequence Claims — Partial Waiver (up to ten sequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Polynucleotide molecules encoding different proteins are normally independent and distinct; absent contrary evidence, each sequence is presumed independent/distinct. The Director has partially waived 37 CFR 1.141 et seq. to permit a reasonable number of such sequences (normally up to ten) to be claimed in a single application without restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Up to ten independent/distinct sequences will generally be examined together; sequences patentably indistinct from selected sequences will also be examined. Sequences encoding the same protein are not considered independent/distinct. Complex cases may require fewer than ten. Applicants may petition under 37 CFR 1.181 for examination of additional sequences by showing they are not independent/distinct. Treatment of combinations differs: combinations of sequences (e.g., multiple SEQ ID Nos.) generally not subject to restriction; examiner searches until one sequence is found allowable or considers combination as a whole. See MPEP § 803.04 and § 1850.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking Claims and Rejoinder
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that 'link' divided inventions (linking claims, generic claims, or subcombination claims) may permit rejoining of previously withdrawn claims when such linking/generic claims become allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a linking or generic claim is allowable and applicant has paid transitional fees, applicant may be notified of fee refund and withdrawn claims may be rejoined. Use form paragraphs 8.42/8.43/8.46/8.47/8.45 as appropriate. Withdrawal of a restriction requirement removes 35 U.S.C. 121 protections; examiners should warn applicants that subsequent continuation/divisional claims might face double patenting rejections. See MPEP §§ 803.03, 821.04 and form-paragraph guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoinder Between Product and Process Inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Process claims that were withdrawn for being non-elected may be rejoined to an allowable product claim only if they depend from or otherwise require all the limitations of the allowable product claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon rejoinder of such process claims, the restriction between elected product and rejoined process(es) is withdrawn. Applicants are encouraged to present dependent process claims early to facilitate rejoinder. Amendments after allowance or final rejection have special treatment (37 CFR 1.312, 1.116). If process claims would raise new issues after rejoinder, applicant may be offered opportunity to cancel process claims or file an RCE. See MPEP § 821.04(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Not Distinct in Plural Applications (Copending Applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two or more applications filed by the same applicant contain conflicting claims, elimination of such claims from all but one application may be required absent good and sufficient reason for retention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should examine claims in each application and may enter provisional double patenting rejections based on conflicting claims; where appropriate, join applications. Use form paragraph 8.29 when conflicting claims are identical or conceded not patentably distinct. See 37 CFR 1.78(b), MPEP § 822 and § 823.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional Double Patenting Rejections for Conflicting Copending Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims in one application are unpatentable over claims in another copending application of the same inventive entity (or commonly owned with different inventors) due to conflicting claims, the examiner should enter 'provisional' double patenting rejections in each application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provisional double patenting rejection should continue in each application while conflicting claims exist in more than one application, unless that provisional double patenting rejection is the only rejection remaining in at least one application. See MPEP § 822 and § 823.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Withdrawal of Restriction Requirement on 35 U.S.C. 121
rubrics_metrics.description: If a restriction requirement is withdrawn, the protections of 35 U.S.C. 121 (e.g., that a patent issued on one divided application cannot be used as a reference against the divisional when filed in time) no longer apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites In re Ziegler and instructs examiners to notify applicants when restriction is withdrawn and warn about potential provisional statutory and/or nonstatutory double patenting rejections for continuation/divisional claims that overlap allowable claims. See MPEP § 821.04 notes and form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone Restriction Practice / Who Should Make the Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on who may make a restriction requirement and when telephone restriction practice may be used (notably in transitional application situations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telephone restriction practice may be used when a normal restriction requirement is appropriate under transitional rules (37 CFR 1.129(b)(1)) and other conditions are met. The application should be brought to Technology Center Special Program Examiner review if transitional exceptions are believed to apply. See MPEP § 803.03 and related notes; signatory authority guidance is in MPEP § 803.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-way Test for Distinctness When Related in Two Ways
rubrics_metrics.description: When plural inventions are capable of being viewed as related in two distinct ways (e.g., both combination/subcombination and genus/species), both applicable criteria for distinctness must be demonstrated to support a restriction requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must apply two-way distinctness tests where required (e.g., combination vs subcombination, related products/processes) and refer to specific MPEP subsections (e.g., § 806.05(c), § 806.05(j)) for examples and tests. See MPEP § 803.01 and § 806 series.
